# Robinhood Stock Prediction After September US Jobs Report
Robinhood Stock traded near $113.24 on October 1 as investors assessed unemployment claims and softer inflation.
Bitcoin price stood around $83,975, while Ethereum (ETH) traded near $2,700 and XRP price hovered at $1.49. The economic combination could support risk appetite, although stronger employment also complicates expectations for lower interest rates.
## **U.S. Initial Jobless Claims came in LOWER than expected this week.**
Initial unemployment claims totaled 197,000 for the week ended September 26, according to the Labor Department. That result undershot the 201,000 forecast reported by Bloomingbit, reinforcing evidence that layoffs remain limited.
The previous reading was revised from 197,000 to 198,000, making the latest result a modest weekly decline. The four-week average fell to 200,000, offering a steadier indication of labor conditions than one weekly reading.

# What’s next for Robinhood stock as valuation concerns remain? - Girls Rock Investing
Robinhood stock has wavered in recent days as investors remain concerned about its steep valuation and slowing growth. HOOD traded at $112.50 on Thursday, slightly below last month’s high of $126.50. So, will the stock retreat or resume its uptrend in October?
## Robinhood is facing headwinds and tailwinds
HOOD stock has wavered amid concerns about its valuation, which remains at an elevated level. Seeking Alpha data shows that its forward price-to-earnings ratio remains at 44, much higher than the sector median of 10. This multiple is also higher than the five-year average of 37.
The company’s other multiples are also substantially higher than the technology and financial sector median. For example, its forward PEG ratio of 2.37 is higher than the sector median of 1.03.
On the positive side, the company has an encouraging rule-of-40 metric, which is calculated by adding its profit margin and its revenue growth. Its net income margin stands at 42%, while its forward revenue growth rate is 17%, giving it a multiple of 59%.
The most recent results showed that Robinhood’s business continued growing, even as its cryptocurrency business dragged. Its net revenue rose by 32% to $1.31 billion, with its transaction and net interest revenues rising to $776 million and $389 million. Robinhood’s net income rose by 48% to $573 million.
The challenge, however, is that its crypto business remained under pressure as the winter continued. Its cryptocurrency revenue dropped by 38% to $100 million as Bitcoin and most altcoins retreated. On the positive side, there are signs that the crypto business is improving.

## What Is The Market Telling Us
Robinhood’s shares are extremely volatile and have had 45 moves greater than 5% over the last year. In that context, today’s move indicates the market considers this news meaningful but not something that would fundamentally change its perception of the business.
The previous big move we wrote about was 8 days ago when the stock dropped 2.7% on the news that reports revealed Meta Platforms is developing a competing prediction markets app.
According to reports, Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg directed a team to build a standalone prediction markets app known as "Arena," sparking fears it could challenge Robinhood's event-contract trading. The news prompted a sector-wide decline, also affecting companies like DraftKings.
Adding to the pressure was a $2 billion convertible note offering, which was announced and priced days earlier. Robinhood intended to use part of the proceeds to repurchase approximately $290 million of its stock and to fund capped call transactions, which are generally expected to reduce potential dilution from the notes' conversion.
Robinhood is down 2.4% since the beginning of the year, and at $112.50 per share, it is trading 26.2% below its 52-week high of $152.46 from October 2025. Investors who bought $1,000 worth of Robinhood’s shares at the IPO in July 2021 would now be looking at an investment worth $3,231.
